p: the Talmud concludes with Maseches Niddah,
and we say, “and Maseches Niddah is concluded,”
for the root of tumah is the tumah of niddah.
And in the pasuk it says (Yechezkel 36:17):
“Like the tumah of a niddah was their way before Me,”
for this is the root of tumah, the contamination of the Nachash.
But in the Midrash (Tanchuma, end of Metzora)
it says that this is to their credit:
“Like the tumah of a niddah, and not like the tumah of a corpse;
for when a dead body is in the house,
אֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל נִכְנָס לְשָׁם וְכוּלֵּי
the Kohen Gadol does not enter there, etc.,
אֲבָל נִדָּה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל נִכְנָס עִמָּהּ וְכוּלֵּי
but with a niddah, the Kohen Gadol enters together with her, etc.
So too, had Hakadosh Baruch Hu
compared them to the tumah of a corpse,
you would say that the Shechinah
rather, He compared them to a niddah,
for the Kohen stands with her in the house, etc.;
so too Hakadosh Baruch Hu, etc.,
‘Who dwells with them in the midst of their tumah.’”
אַף שֶׁבָּא עַל תִּיקּוּן פְּגַם חַוָּה
even though it came to rectify the flaw of Chavah,
as Chazal say in the Gemara (Shabbos 31b),
“she is stricken in the chambers of her womb,”
and in the Midrash (Tanchuma, beginning of Noach, and there in Metzora):
let her guard her niddah and let her blood be spilled,
so that she may be atoned for, etc.” —
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִיתָא בַּמִּשְׁנָה (נִדָּה סד, ב)
nevertheless, it says in the Mishnah (Niddah 64b):
כָּל גֶּפֶן יֵשׁ בּוֹ יַיִן כּוּלֵּי
“Every vine has wine in it, etc.,”
and in the Gemara: “Just as leaven is good for dough,
so is blood good for a woman, etc.;
כָּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁדָּמֶיהָ מְרוּבִּין בָּנֶיהָ מְרוּבִּין,
any woman whose blood is abundant, her children are abundant.”
The yetzer hara, too, is compared
in the Gemara (Berachos 17a) to the leaven in the dough,
and leaven, too, is good in small measure,
as Chazal say in the Gemara (Berachos 34a);
but here they said, “her blood is abundant.”
And any woman who has no
blood of besulim or blood of niddah
is called a durkti, a barren one;
and this is among the first of the curses,
of the ten curses with which Chavah was cursed:
blood of besulim and blood of niddah
And it appears that they derived it from the pasuk,
that from this, since her blood is abundant, her children are abundant.
corresponds to the ten holy middos
and it corresponds to the Ten Utterances of Creation.
for when it is refined through teshuvah
“If your sins are like these years,
which have been arranged and coming since the six days of Creation,
they shall be made white as snow”;
and there it was light out of darkness.
And it is like Torah she'b'al peh,
which was given to rectify the “much anger,”
they would have been given only
כִּי בְּרוֹב חָכְמָה רוֹב כָּעַס (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח),
‘For in much wisdom is much anger’” (Koheles 1:18).
Therefore it is compared to a vine with wine,
which is the wine of the Torah she'b'al peh
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רעא, ב,
for here too the much anger
And likewise is the first curse,
and through it, “I will greatly increase,”
that her children will be abundant.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַשְּׂאוֹר יָפֶה לָעִיסָּה
And this is what they said, “Just as leaven is good for dough,”
for through it they merited much wisdom;
“so is blood good for a woman,”
And we find in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Noach 2):
“The Torah, in which it is written,
פְּרִי צַדִּיק עֵץ חַיִּים (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל)
‘The fruit of the tzaddik is a tree of life’ (Mishlei 11:30) —
בָּנִים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר אֶלָּא פְּרִי צַדִּיק
it does not say ‘children,’ but ‘the fruit of the tzaddik’;
and likewise, the offspring of a person
The words of Torah are the fruit and the offspring.
And this is why they concluded the Talmud with Maseches Niddah
which deals with blood of besulim;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּא עַל יְדֵי קִלְלַת חַוָּה
and nevertheless it came through the curse of Chavah;
And so we find that Knesses Yisrael
is compared, in praise, to a besulah,
that the matter of the tumah of niddah will be rectified,
so that there will be only the small measure,
the leaven in the dough, which is good in small measure.
וְהִנֵּה רַבִּי מֵאִיר דָּרַשׁ (נִדָּה לא, ב)
that a niddah is for seven days, etc.?
So that she be as beloved to her husband
as at the time she entered the chuppah,”
and that is for the good.
And likewise we find in the holy Zohar
מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ וְכוּלֵּי (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ מג, ד)
“‘Since you are precious in My eyes, you are honored, etc.’ (Yeshayahu 43:4).
It should have said yekar, ‘precious,’ etc.;
This implies that he became precious through himself, etc.;
דְּהָא לֵית רְחִימָא לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
for Kudsha Brich Hu has no beloved one
except one who has returned from his sins, etc.”
And as in the parable he brings of a prince
who was taken captive and redeemed from his captivity,
who is more esteemed and beloved before the king
than one who was always with him.
And this is exactly as we said:
that through the leaven in the dough
הוּא חָבִיב וְחָשׁוּב לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
a person is beloved and esteemed before Hashem Yisbarach
כְּשֶׁמְּתַקֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי תְשׁוּבָה
when he afterwards rectifies it through teshuvah;
like the matter of the tumah of niddah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה חֲבִיבָה עַל בַּעְלָהּ
through which she is beloved to her husband
as at the time she entered the chuppah.
And this is as Chazal say (Berachos 34b):
“In the place where baalei teshuvah stand,
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג טז, ב)
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 16b):
“They are established in a higher place, etc.”
This means that they are from the first utterance:
“If your sins are like the years, etc.,
from the six days of Creation.”
And in the utterance of Bereishis darkness is mentioned,
for there is no light except that
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
the comparison to the tumah of niddah,
which is the root of the flaw,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא רִיבּוּי בָּנִים וְכָאָמוּר.
and through it comes an abundance of children, as stated.
And this is why they concluded the Talmud with Maseches Niddah,
they will rectify the first flaw,
and there will remain only the small measure of leaven
that is good for the dough;
and that through this Yisrael will be
“Since you are precious in My eyes, you are honored,”
for he became precious through himself,
and through this, “I have loved you.”
